You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Compare the bars’ vertical run lengths between panels: demonstrated example has color-2 lengths 1 vs 2 (difference 1), color-4 lengths 2 vs 4 (difference 2), producing a 2x2 output filled with color 4. Patches can have varying sizes; do not instead remove the smallest patch by area.'), ('arc_task_11174e1e_overlay_binary_halves_with_color_3', 'ARC task-11174e1e: overlay binary halves with color 3', 'For ARC task-11174e1e, input is 9x5: top 4x5 contains 0/2, middle row is all 4, bottom 4x5 contains 0/1. All components (including color-8 cells) slide right simultaneously until blocked by the grid edge or another component. Continue until no component can move; preserve shapes/colors and leave zeros elsewhere. Confirmed by demo: individual pieces translated right into a tightly packed arrangement without overlap; test solved correctly with this rule.'), ('arc_task_570417a6_expand_occupied_cells_using_empty_cell_mask', 'ARC task-570417a6: expand occupied cells using empty-cell mask', 'For task-570417a6, the input is a 3x3 grid with background 0 and a single nonzero color. For each nonzero input cell, put the nonzero color in the positions within its 3x3 block corresponding to ZERO cells in the original 3x3 input mask; put zeros at positions corresponding to occupied cells. Compare occupied-cell masks position by position. If the masks are disjoint, output the cellwise overlay in a 4x4 grid, retaining each panel’s color (demos 1 and 3). If any position is occupied in both panels, output only the left 4x4 panel unchanged; discard the right pattern (demo 2 and solved test). Do not include the separator column. Evidence: demo1 disjoint, merged output; demo3 disjoint, merged output; demo2 has overlaps and output equals left; test overlaps and correct output was left panel.'), ('arc_task_51335a5e_move_closed_outlines_to_top_and_open_shapes_to_bottom', 'ARC task-51335a5e: move closed outlines to top and open shapes to bottom', 'For ARC task-51335a5e, identify 4-connected colored components. When same-side objects overlap in column ranges, pack without overlap, keeping their original vertical order (top-side objects top-to-bottom; bottom-side objects top-to-bottom), so they touch/stack. Translate by the component bounding box, not by recoloring. Important common pitfall: count exact bounding-box height and preserve all edge rows of shapes; the 5x5 frame has top and bottom full rows with three intermediate side-only rows. Demonstrations show output dimensions unchanged and all shapes retain original horizontal positions.')]
